import os
import subprocess
import sys

from sase.vcs_provider import get_vcs_provider

checkout_target = {{ setup.checkout_target | tojson }}
project_name = {{ setup.project_name | tojson }}
gh_ref = {{ gh_ref | tojson }}

provider = get_vcs_provider(os.getcwd())

# Checkout the PR branch so that subsequent diffs are relative to the
# PR tip rather than the default branch. Try checkout_target first
# (works for default-branch refs like origin/main), then fall back to
# Patch name -> branch name conversion.
is_patch = checkout_target == f"origin/{gh_ref}"
ok, err = provider.checkout(checkout_target, os.getcwd())
if not ok:
    if is_patch:
        # Patch ref — resolve name to branch name
        resolved = provider.resolve_revision(
            gh_ref, project_name, os.getcwd()
        )
        ok, err = provider.checkout(resolved, os.getcwd())
    else:
        # Project/repo ref — try common default branch names
        for fallback in ["master", "main"]:
            ok, err = provider.checkout(fallback, os.getcwd())
            if ok:
                break
    if not ok:
        print(
            f"Warning: checkout failed: {err}",
            file=sys.stderr,
        )

# Sync with remote after checkout
subprocess.run(
    ["git", "pull", "--rebase", "--quiet"],
    capture_output=True,
    text=True,
    check=False,
)

# Record HEAD for the diff step
result = subprocess.run(
    ["git", "rev-parse", "HEAD"],
    capture_output=True,
    text=True,
    check=False,
)
head = result.stdout.strip() if result.returncode == 0 else ""
print(f"head_before={head}")
print("success=true")

head_before="{{ checkout.head_before }}"
if [ -z "$head_before" ]; then
  exit 0
fi
head_now=$(git rev-parse HEAD)
diff_dir="${SASE_TMPDIR:-${SASE_HOME:-$HOME/.sase}/tmp}/gh-diffs"
mkdir -p "$diff_dir"
diff_file=$(mktemp "$diff_dir/sase-gh-XXXXXX.diff")
if [ "$head_now" != "$head_before" ]; then
  # Commits were made — show only the last commit's diff
  git diff HEAD~1 HEAD > "$diff_file" 2>/dev/null
  commit_msg=$(git log -1 --format='%s' HEAD)
  echo "meta_commit_message=$commit_msg"
else
  # No commits — show uncommitted changes
  git diff HEAD > "$diff_file" 2>/dev/null
  git ls-files --others --exclude-standard -z 2>/dev/null \
    | while IFS= read -r -d '' f; do
        git diff --no-index /dev/null "$f" 2>/dev/null
      done >> "$diff_file"
fi
if [ -s "$diff_file" ]; then
  echo "diff_path=$diff_file"
else
  rm -f "$diff_file"
fi

# Stash any uncommitted changes (including untracked files)
if ! git diff --quiet HEAD 2>/dev/null || [ -n "$(git ls-files --others --exclude-standard)" ]; then
  git stash push --include-untracked -m "gh-workflow-$(date +%s)" --quiet
  echo "stashed=true"
else
  echo "stashed=false"
fi
git fetch origin --quiet 2>&1 || true
git pull --rebase --quiet 2>/dev/null || true
echo "success=true"

from sase_github.scripts.gh_setup import main
main(
    gh_ref={{ gh_ref | tojson }},
    n={{ n | tojson }},
    release={{ release | tojson }},
    workflow_label={{ workflow_label | tojson }},
)

Opened the research repo and read the lead's report plus the diagram manifest (status ready, 2 diagrams, source matches). Next I'll draft the restructured canonical file.

Now validating: inventory checks, anchors via pandoc, and table/URL survival.

Published and registered. Now finishing the turn through the final declaration.

I published the lead's bank badge report as the canonical `202611/bank_badge_strip_family/bank_badge_strip_family.md` and registered it as artifact `file:explicit:dae7530e459fd1ea44cb2ee1` (label `research:202611/bank_badge_strip_family/bank_badge_strip_family.md`). The commit to the research repo is declared and runs after this turn ends.

**Source:** there was exactly one matching report, `research:202611/bank_badge_strip_family/bank_badge_strip_family__final.md`. I didn't modify it, the drafts, or the diagram manifest. The diagram manifest had status `ready` with 2 diagrams, and its `source` matched the lead's label.

**Opening order:** title, then a two-sentence research query blockquote, then the infographic (`bank_badge_strip_family_infographic.png`, which exists beside the report), then `## Bottom line` (the lead's Verdict).

**Section order:** Adjustments to the requirements, What exists today (verified), Where the five reports disagreed, Design spec, Data contract, Glossary strand, Implementation order, Open questions for Bryan, Recommended solution, Sources and method. The lead's note listing its five input reports now sits in Sources and method.

**Editorial changes:**
- I removed the hand numbers from headings.
- I moved the parenthetical notes out of headings into each section's first line (for example "The big one." and "All comparisons on integer cents.").
- Moving the adjustments table up made two of its "see above" pointers wrong. I changed "§Color above" and "§Waiting above" to "below" and made both links.
- I turned the lead's § references and a few summary points into in-document links.

A script check confirmed the text is otherwise the lead's, word for word, once those link and direction edits are set aside. Every table cell and both code blocks are present.

**Diagrams accepted (2; mermaid fences: lead 0 + 2 = 2):**
- `period-routing` → `#figure-period-routing`, placed after the CLI shape resolution paragraph.
- `shared-rendering` → `#figure-shared-rendering`, placed after the Data contract "Plugin side" paragraph.

Each figure sits in its own anchor `<div>` with the fence copied byte-for-byte and the manifest caption, and has one reference sentence linking to it. None were omitted.

**Links:** there are no external URLs, so none were unrepairable. The five relative links to the draft reports and the infographic all resolve in the report's folder. Every in-document link, including both figure anchors, matched an ID in pandoc's HTML output.
